title: Sermon notes
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: Farewell Pilgrimage, hadith and fiqh
source: Written for islamic-studies/y9 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: sermon notes)
intro: Lesson 20: The Farewell Sermon: life, property and the end of riba. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Bukhari and Muslim
paras: Your blood and your wealth are sacred to you, like the sacredness of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours.

panels.title: Ending the old ways
points: Blood feuds of the time of ignorance are ended
Riba of the time of ignorance is ended
He began with his own family's claims

panels.title: Riba in Islam
points: Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba (2:275)
Islamic finance shares profit and risk
Interest is taught as knowledge, never to take

keywords.def: interest or usury, forbidden in Islam

questions.q: Explain why the Prophet ﷺ ended blood feuds.
questions.a: They caused endless revenge killings; ending them protected life and united the community.

questions.q: Which ayah says trade is permitted and riba forbidden?
Sermon notes on the pupil PDF: for each message (life, property, feuds, riba) write the meaning, why it mattered then, and one example of it today.
questions.a: Accurate meanings, context and modern examples (e.g. knife crime, theft, payday loans)

questions.q: Extend: why start with his own family's claims?
questions.a: To lead by example and show the rule applies to everyone.

questions.q: Stretch: how does Islamic finance avoid riba?
questions.a: Sharing profit and risk (musharakah) or a fixed cost-plus sale (murabahah).

questions.q: Why compare life and wealth to the sacred day?
options: To show they must never be violated
questions.a: A) To show they must never be violated. The day, month and city were all sacred; so are a Muslim's life and property.

questions.q: Think again: why start with life and property?
questions.a: They are the basis of a just and safe society.
